## Step 1: Develop initial scraper and crawler


```{python}
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import pandas as pd

url = "https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/enforcement/"
html = requests.get(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"}).text
soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")

cards = soup.select("li.usa-card")
rows = []

for card in cards:
    a = card.select_one("h2.usa-card__heading a")
    if not a:
        continue

    title = a.get_text(strip=True)
    link = "https://oig.hhs.gov" + a["href"]

    date_tag = card.select_one("span.text-base-dark.padding-right-105")
    date = date_tag.get_text(strip=True) if date_tag else None

    cat_tag = card.select_one("ul.display-inline.add-list-reset li")
    category = cat_tag.get_text(strip=True) if cat_tag else None

    rows.append({
        "title": title,
        "date": date,
        "category": category,
        "link": link
    })

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
df.head()


```

HTML inspection showed that each enforcement action is contained within an li tag with class usa-card, with the title in an h2 heading, the date in a span element, and the category listed within an inline unordered list - ul tag.

## Step 2: Making the scraper dynamic

### 1. Turning the scraper into a function 

* a. Pseudo-Code
Define function scrape_enforcement_actions(start_year, start_month, run_scraper)

If start_year < 2013, print warning message and exit function

If run_scraper is False, exit function without scraping

Create start_date using start_year and start_month

Initialize empty list rows

Set page = 1

While True:

Build URL for current page using page number

Request webpage and parse HTML

Select all enforcement action cards on the page

If no cards are found, break loop

For each card on the page:

Extract title and link

Extract date and convert to datetime

Extract category

If date is on or after start_date, add row to rows

Keep track of dates seen on this page

If the oldest date on the page is earlier than start_date, break loop

Increment page by 1

Pause for 1 second

Convert rows into a dataframe

Save dataframe as enforcement_actions_year_month.csv

Return dataframe


* b. Create Dynamic Scraper


```{python}

import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import pandas as pd
import time

def scrape_enforcement_actions(start_year: int,
                               start_month: int,
                               run_scraper: bool = True) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    if start_year < 2013:
        print("Please restrict to year >= 2013 (only actions after 2013 are listed).")
        return None

    if not run_scraper:
        print("run_scraper=False, skipping web scraping.")
        return None

    start_date = pd.Timestamp(start_year, start_month, 1)

    base_url = "https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/enforcement/"
    headers = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"}

    rows = []
    page = 1

    while True:
        page_url = base_url if page == 1 else f"{base_url}?page={page}"
        resp = requests.get(page_url, headers=headers, timeout=30)
        soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "html.parser")

        cards = soup.select("li.usa-card")
        if not cards:
            break

        page_dates = []

        for card in cards:
            a = card.select_one("h2.usa-card__heading a[href^='/fraud/enforcement/']")
            if not a:
                continue

            title = a.get_text(strip=True)
            link = "https://oig.hhs.gov" + a["href"]
            date_tag = card.select_one("span.text-base-dark.padding-right-105")
            date = date_tag.get_text(strip=True) if date_tag else None
            date_dt = pd.to_datetime(date, format="%B %d, %Y", errors="coerce") if date else pd.NaT
            if pd.isna(date_dt):
                continue
            cat_tag = card.select_one("ul.display-inline.add-list-reset li")
            category = cat_tag.get_text(strip=True) if cat_tag else None

            page_dates.append(date_dt)

            if date_dt >= start_date:
                rows.append({"title": title, "date": date, "category": category, "link": link})
        if page_dates and min(page_dates) < start_date:
            break

        page += 1
        time.sleep(1)

    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)

    required_name = f"enforcement_actions_{start_year}_{start_month:02d}.csv"
    df.to_csv(required_name, index=False)

    print(f"Saved {len(df)} rows to {required_name}")
    return df

```

```{python}
RUN_SCRAPER = True
df_actions = scrape_enforcement_actions(2024, 1, run_scraper=RUN_SCRAPER)

```

```{python}
df_actions.head()

```

Starting from January 2024, the dynamic scraper collected 1787 enforcement actions in total. The earliest was dated January 3, 2024 and titled “Former Nurse Aide Indicted in Death of Clarksville …”, which falls under the State Enforcement Agencies category.

## Step 3: Plot data based on scraped data

### 1. Plot the number of enforcement actions over time

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import altair as alt

df = pd.read_csv("enforcement_actions_2022_01.csv")
```

```{python}
df["date_dt"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])

monthly_counts = (
    df
    .assign(month_year=df["date_dt"].dt.to_period("M").dt.to_timestamp())
    .groupby("month_year")
    .size()
    .reset_index(name="n_actions")
)

```

```{python}
alt.Chart(monthly_counts).mark_line(point=True).encode(
    alt.X("month_year:T", title="Month"),
    alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of Enforcement Actions"),
).properties(
    title="HHS OIG Enforcement Actions Over Time (Since January 2022)"
)

```



### 2. Plot the number of enforcement actions categorized:

* based on "Criminal and Civil Actions" vs. "State Enforcement Agencies"

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import altair as alt

df = pd.read_csv("enforcement_actions_2022_01.csv")
df["date_dt"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])
df["month_year"] = df["date_dt"].dt.to_period("M").dt.to_timestamp()
cat_df = df[df["category"].isin([
    "Criminal and Civil Actions",
    "State Enforcement Agencies"
])]
cat_monthly = (
    cat_df
    .groupby(["month_year", "category"])
    .size()
    .reset_index(name="n_actions")
)

alt.Chart(cat_monthly).mark_line(point=True).encode(
    alt.X("month_year:T", title="Month"),
    alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of Enforcement Actions"),
    color=alt.Color("category:N", title="Category")
).properties(
    title="Enforcement Actions Over Time by Category (Since Jan 2022)"
)

```

* based on five topics

```{python}
cca = df[df["category"] == "Criminal and Civil Actions"].copy()
def classify_topic(title):
    t = title.lower()

    if any(k in t for k in ["health", "medicare", "medicaid", "hospital", "physician", "doctor", "clinic"]):
        return "Health Care Fraud"
    elif any(k in t for k in ["bank", "financial", "loan", "wire fraud", "tax", "money laundering"]):
        return "Financial Fraud"
    elif any(k in t for k in ["drug", "opioid", "controlled substance", "pharmacy"]):
        return "Drug Enforcement"
    elif any(k in t for k in ["bribe", "bribery", "kickback", "corruption"]):
        return "Bribery/Corruption"
    else:
        return "Other"

cca["topic"] = cca["title"].apply(classify_topic)
topic_monthly = (
    cca
    .groupby(["month_year", "topic"])
    .size()
    .reset_index(name="n_actions")
)

alt.Chart(topic_monthly).mark_line(point=False).encode(
    alt.X("month_year:T", title="Month"),
    alt.Y("n_actions:Q", title="Number of Enforcement Actions"),
    color=alt.Color("topic:N", title="Topic")
).properties(
    title="Criminal & Civil Enforcement Actions by Topic (Since Jan 2022)"
)

```
